author: ImCK
body: The priority should always be to seize opportunities for expansion and growth. As shareholders, we understand that reinvesting profits into strategic growth is key. However, if we're talking about rewarding shareholders without burdening the company with high financing costs, then the best approach is for management to adopt a Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP). Why let the banks earn 6% in interest when shareholders are willing to reinvest dividends back into the company? A DRP not only reduces financing costs but also allows shareholders to increase their stake — more shares, more long-term wealth. Even if the share price moves sideways during the expansion phase, we're growing our ownership and compounding returns. It’s a win-win — the company strengthens its balance sheet, and shareholders benefit through increased equity over time. but too bad management like dont know use this tool .

author: Joe18
body: * NICE's previous stance on Leqembi: NICE's rejection of Leqembi based on cost-effectiveness sets a precedent. For HMTM to gain NHS approval, it would almost certainly need to demonstrate a more favorable cost-benefit ratio. In summary: * Leqembi (Lecanemab): Approved by MHRA, but not recommended by NICE for NHS use due to high cost relative to benefit. US list price is around $26,500/year (approx. £20,000/year), with significant associated administration costs. * TauRx (HMTM): Pending MHRA approval. If approved, it is anticipated to be cheaper than Leqembi, primarily due to its oral administration and the company's stated goal of affordability, which would be crucial for NHS adoption given NICE's previous decisions. We will have to await the MHRA's decision on HMTM and, if approved, the subsequent NICE assessment to get a clear picture of its cost and availability on the NHS.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: Malaysia has agreed to reduce tariffs on 98.4% of US products as a result of negotiations to get a lower tariff, according to Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. In speaking about the tariff barrier aspect of Malaysia’s offer to the US, Zafrul outlined that Malaysia offered a reduction or elimination of 11,260 out of 11,444 tariff lines. “We made a comprehensive offer that covers 98% of all tariff lines. There are many tariff lines,” Zafrul told the press on Friday. Meanwhile, of these 11,260 products Malaysia agreed to reduce tariffs on, tariffs on 6,911 or 61% have been eliminated. Zafrul noted that Malaysia’s existing tariff lines with 0% duty already stood at 6,567, mostly comprising industrial products. In essence, Malaysia exempted tariffs on an additional 344 tariff lines. He underlined the US had requested for levies on 191 agricultural products and 1,347 industrial products to be removed. A Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry spokesperson said the figures are still indicative and will be finalised in a joint statement. On the other side, Zafrul noted the US is open to removing tariffs on upstream agricultural goods or commodities, or on goods that cannot be produced domestically in the US — such as cocoa, rubber and palm oil. The full list of the new tariff lines is set to be released later. Zafrul said a joint statement between Miti and the US Trade Representative will be issued over the weekend to disclose further details of the tariff deal. Semiconductor, pharmaceutical product exemptions remain Meanwhile, Zafrul clarified that US import tariff exemptions for Malaysian semiconductor and pharmaceutical products will remain. Sector-specific tariffs under Section 232 of the US Trade Expansion Act are currently undergoing a study on fairness, slated for completion in December. Until then, it is understood that the status quo will remain for sector-specific tariffs.

New attractions and enhanced facilities During a recent visit to Singapore, Spencer Lee, executive VP of sales, marketing and PR at RWG, announced that Eufloria, a new mega glasshouse attraction themed around the four seasons, will soft-launch in January 2026. RWG currently offers 10,500 hotel rooms across seven properties. The resort also boasts two theme parks, a premium outlet mall, two cable car lines, and a live entertainment arena. In June, it hosted Malaysia’s largest outdoor music festival, welcoming 12,000 Heineken guests. author: ImCK
body: How stablecoin issuers make money: They hold reserves (e.g., USD) for every token issued. Instead of letting that cash sit idle, they invest it in short-term U.S. Treasuries or similar safe assets that yield ~4–5%+ per year. Example: If you issue $10B worth of stablecoins and invest the reserves at 5%, that’s $500M annual interest income — without touching principal. Why it feels like “free money”: The users aren’t paid interest — they just use the stablecoin for transactions, trading, or gaming credits — but the issuer keeps the yield from the reserves. For Genting specifically: Immediate benefit: Could improve liquidity and generate predictable cash flow to service or refinance debt. Gaming synergy: Stablecoin could double as both a payment method in their ecosystem (casinos, resorts, online gaming) and a DeFi product for external markets. Regulatory hurdle: Financial regulators + gaming regulators would be very cautious, especially since Genting already sits in a highly scrutinized industry. Actually, Tether (USDT) is already earning billions a year this way. In Q1 2024 alone, they reported over $1B profit just from Treasury interest — and they don’t run a single casino. If Genting combined casino float + stablecoin float, they could have a financial engine even stronger than their gaming tables.

author: Joe18
body: Genting Malaysia Berhad (GENM), through its subsidiary Empire Resorts Inc, has entered into a significant agreement with the Sullivan County Resort Facilities Local Development Corporation (SCRFLDC) concerning its non-gaming assets in New York. The arrangement is a part of a larger plan to restructure and strengthen Empire Resorts' financial position. Here are the key details of the arrangement: 1. Disposal of Non-Gaming Assets: * Empire Resorts will sell its non-gaming assets to SCRFLDC for US$525 million (approximately RM2.2 billion). * These assets include: * The 332-room Resorts World Catskills (RWC) hotel. * The 99-room Alder Hotel. * The 18-hole Monster Golf Course. * The 2,500-seat RWC Epicenter. * Multiple restaurants. 2. Management Agreement: * Following the sale, Empire Resorts will enter into a 20-year management agreement with SCRFLDC to continue managing all the non-gaming assets it just sold. * This management agreement includes an automatic renewal for two successive five-year periods, extending the potential management period. 3. Land Lease: * Simultaneously, Empire Resorts will enter into a land lease with SCRFLDC for all the land on which these non-gaming assets are built. * The land lease agreement will be in effect until February 15, 2066. 4. Use of Proceeds: * The proceeds from the disposal of the non-gaming assets will be used to: * Purchase 1,554.6 acres of land from a real estate investment trust (EPR Properties) for US$201.3 million (RM848.1 million). This acquisition is intended to strengthen Genting Malaysia's asset base and provide long-term control over the land where the RWC's gaming and non-gaming facilities are located, as well as vacant land for future development. * Redeem US$300 million (RM1.3 billion) in 7.75% senior unsecured notes due in November 2026, which will make Empire Resorts debt-free. * Fund working capital needs, generating about US$10 million (RM42.1 million) in surplus cash for general working capital. This strategic move allows Genting Malaysia to offload non-gaming assets while retaining operational control and strengthening its financial and competitive position in the New York market.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: First public hearing on Resorts World’s casino gaming license bid draws community support Posted on August 21, 2025

author: Michaelchan2024
body: More than 40 people testified in support of Resorts World NYC receiving its casino gaming license during a public advisory hearing at Queens Borough Hall on Wednesday, Aug. 20. The hearing was led by the Resorts World New York City Community Advisory Committee, chaired by Assembly Member Stacey Pheffer Amato. Committee members include Queens Borough President Donovan Richards, Community Board 10 Chairperson Betty Bratton, state Sen. James Sanders, Stevens Martinez, Deputy Director of Intergovernmental Affairs on Long Island for Gov. Kathy Hochul, and Nicole Garcia, Queens Borough Commissioner of NYC DOT. Resorts World NYC, located at 110-00 Rockaway Blvd, has operated as the city’s only casino since opening in 2011 and is currently applying for one of three downstate full gaming licenses that were approved through state legislation. Resorts World’s $5.5 billion proposal aims to expand the casino’s existing 73-acre space into a global entertainment destination. Plans include creating a 350,000-square-foot meeting, conference, and entertainment space, a 7,000-seat multi-use arena, a gaming floor approximately 500,000 square feet, and approximately 30 new food and beverage options. Upon completion, the gaming floor would be the largest in the U.S. with 6,000 slots and electronic table games and 800 live table games. Additionally, the campus would expand its hotel capacity to 2,000 rooms and hold a STEM innovation center.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: If selected, the RWNYC site would generate over 10,000 jobs, including 5,000 unionized construction jobs and 5,000 permanent jobs, and 3,000 units of on-site workforce housing. In addition to the 10,000 construction jobs, RWNYC is expected to create another 14,000 indirect and induced jobs. Community support Community leaders, including southeast Queens elected officials Council Member Nantasha Williams and Assembly Member Khaleel Anderson, testified during the hearing. Anderson said that he conditionally supports Resorts World’s pursuit of a casino gaming license. “Resorts World has done well, the property looks great, and the proposal is outstanding; however, we want to see more investment directly into physical infrastructure in the surrounding community,” Anderson said.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: Anderson proposed the creation of a $140 million community investment fund, as well as investing in mental health and addiction services. “Of course, we know gambling is an addictive sport, and we’d like to see physical in-community assets. Assets that represent the casino in the community, not on the casino property, but a footprint in the community. I believe that $140 million community investment fund would do just that,” he said. Williams ms expressed how Resorts World has been a strong partner in supporting workforce development within Queens’ communities. “I am particularly grateful for Resorts World’s focus on the future, as they partner with York College to provide workforce development programs in my district and train and prepare residents, building skills and creating career opportunities that will likely benefit the community,” Williams said. “The jobs created by Resorts World bring real economic benefits to our neighborhoods. Residents gain stable employment and opportunities for career growth.”

author: ImCK
body: B2C model To attract traffic, you often need to keep lowering prices or offering promotions. This constant price competition squeezes gross profit margins, and you also have to keep spending on marketing to sustain attention. Customer loyalty is harder to maintain, and the cost of acquisition is high. B2B model You don’t need flashy patterns like MLM-style attraction. If you secure the right corporate or organizational partners (e.g., venue hosts, associations), they can bring in thousands of quality members or spenders at once. This gives you a more stable and higher-value customer base, without continuous price wars.

body: Index provider MSCI Friday said it has removed three Malaysian stocks from the MSCI Malaysia Index in its latest quarterly review of equity indexes. Genting, PPB Group, and Sime Darby will cease to be part of the MSCI Malaysia Index after the close of trading on Aug. 26

author: ImCK
body: 1. What MSCI does MSCI is an index provider. Its indexes (like MSCI World, MSCI Emerging Markets, MSCI Malaysia) are benchmarks for global investors. Trillions of dollars in passive funds and ETFs (index funds) track MSCI indexes. 2. Why inclusion/removal matters If a stock is in the MSCI Malaysia Index, funds that track the index must hold it. If MSCI removes a stock, index-tracking funds are forced to sell it. This can cause selling pressure and short-term volatility around the effective date.

author: ImCK
body: 😃who is the man behind this Here’s what 5% shareholding can do: Requisition an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) A shareholder or group holding ≥5% of the paid-up capital with voting rights can formally require the company to call an EGM (outside the AGM) to discuss specific matters. Propose Resolutions at AGM/EGM With 5% you can request that certain resolutions be placed on the agenda for the AGM/EGM. This allows you to table issues management may not want to raise. Circulate Statements to Shareholders Shareholders holding ≥5% can request the company to circulate statements related to proposed resolutions or matters to be discussed, at the company’s expense. Call an EGM Yourself (if Board fails) If the Board doesn’t act within the required time after a valid 5% requisition, the shareholder(s) can call the meeting themselves. Influence Voting Outcome (in close cases) While 5% alone cannot block an ordinary resolution (which needs >50%) or a special resolution (which needs ≥75%), in practice, a 5% block can be powerful if other shareholders are fragmented or passive. Regulatory Recognition Bursa and SC (Securities Commission) recognize 5% as a substantial shareholding level. Any crossing of this threshold requires disclosure (Form 29A in Malaysia). This gives visibility and sometimes negotiation leverage with management. In short: 5% is not enough to control Genting, but it is enough to force management to listen because you can demand meetings, propose resolutions, and rally other shareholders.

author: Daim88
body: PETALING JAYA: Genting Plantations Bhd, which posted higher revenue and profitability for the second quarter ended June 30, 2025 (2Q25), as well as for first half of the year (1H25), anticipates palm product prices to remain stable in the near term. This outlook is supported by improved export momentum, thanks to price competitiveness against soybean oil. Additionally, higher biodiesel mandates in Indonesia, Brazil, and the United States are also helping support prices. Nonetheless, the plantation group said that seasonally higher production and the absence of festive-driven demand, coupled with ongoing uncertainties surrounding trade policies, may limit the upside potential for prices. “Barring any weather anomalies, the group expects fresh fruit bunch production to improve in the remaining months of the year underpinned by anticipated crop recovery and progression of existing mature areas into higher yielding brackets in Indonesia,” Genting Plantations said in a statement. In the 2Q25, its net profit came in at RM192.57mil, bringing 1H25 figure to RM253.83mil. Revenue stood at RM766.99mil, while 1H25 revenue reached RM1.49bil.

author: ImCK
body: Nevada regulators are preparing to loosen restrictions on casino salons, private gaming rooms designed to cater to high-value patrons, in an effort to reverse slowing tourism and keep the state competitive. The Nevada Gaming Control Board (NGCB) has endorsed a sweeping set of amendments (pdf) to its two-decade-old salon rules. These changes—now awaiting a final vote from the Nevada Gaming Commission in late September—would lower financial entry thresholds, introduce poker as a salon option, and give casinos more flexibility in setting their own standards. For Chair Mike Dreitzer, the motivation behind the changes is clear: “The goals remain the same. Bringing more revenue to the state of Nevada in uncertain times and allowing for flexible and unique amenities that certain non-restricted licensees offer their valued patrons. All of this is in the face of growing competition across the U.S. and the world.” From High-Rollers Only to Wider Accessibility Salons were first authorized in 2001 to draw wealthy gamblers who preferred privacy after 9/11 created economic turbulence for Nevada. At the time, players needed to front $500,000 in cash or credit to enter. That barrier was reduced to $300,000 during the Great Recession of 2008, but salons remained the exclusive domain of major Strip resorts. The NGCB now recommends cutting the deposit requirement dramatically, from $300,000 to just $20,000. Casinos could also request permission to set their own minimums, with the Board chair able to grant exceptions for certain properties or customers. This shift, according to Dreitzer, is about balancing exclusivity with accessibility: enough of a threshold to preserve the salon experience, but low enough to attract new types of players. Virginia Valentine, president and CEO of the Nevada Resort Association (NRA), called the lowered minimums “the most significant impact in the legislation,” arguing that Nevada had placed itself at a disadvantage compared with other jurisdictions by requiring such high entry costs. “By lowering the minimum front-money requirements while offering the same privacy, security, and elevated gaming experience, we believe we’ll attract casino patrons who aren’t playing here now,” she said, according to CDC Gaming. Poker and Expanded Offerings One of the most notable changes is the proposed inclusion of poker in salons. Industry leaders have long argued that high-stakes card games are thriving in California card rooms and underground markets, and Nevada is missing out. Under the plan, poker games in salons would require a $20,000 table minimum, with each player contributing at least $10,000. Unlike traditional salon play, every participant—not just the host—would undergo financial checks. Senior Deputy Attorney General John Michela emphasized poker’s potential, stating that moving such play from private homes into regulated casinos could generate “significant revenue for Nevada.”

author: magellan
body: MSCI exclusion day closing match 140m done at 2.80 were largely bought by opportunist arbitrage funds, while passive ETFs following MSCI exited. Genting is a gaming stock, there are no Islamic compliant (EPF, KWAP, mutual funds, insurance funds etc) who will buy and hold for long term on that day. These 140m buyers are mostly opportunistic arbitrage funds who will simply sell when there is a small 3 to 9 sen arbitrage trading profit (1% to 3% trading profit over the short term). That is why we are seeing so many sellers suddenly appearing and flooding the market with massive sell orders. These 140m shares can be slowly sold over a period of about 1.5 months (30+ trading days) assuming these arbitrage funds are selling about 5 - 7m shares daily. Hence, expect share price to recover only in November after those opportunistic arbitrage funds fully exited all their 140m shares.

author: ImCK
body: Strong arguments for Resorts World NYC To the east at the Queens Borough Hall, Resorts World NYC also fielded its second hearing, about three weeks after receiving unanimous support from community groups and nonprofits at its first meeting in mid-August. Monday saw another three-hour display of support without a single dissenter. Prior to the comment period, Resorts World Chief Legal and Strategy Officer Kevin Jones gave another passionate presentation, stressing the strengths of the proposal. These include a significant speed to market advantage, both for the casino and community benefits; an established site; local operating expertise; and completed labour and zoning agreements. It has been considered a frontrunner in the New York casino race since the beginning, for those reasons. If licensed, the property now containing video lottery terminals would transition to a commercial casino while concurrently embarking on a phased, $5.5 billion expansion. The property opened as a VLT facility in 2011 and has contributed billions in state taxes since then. Even without a full licence, it consistently ranks as one of the top-grossing casinos in the US, with annual revenue approaching $1 billion. “We achieved all of this while reducing crime in our neighbourhood, increasing land values, improving the quality of life, while staying at the forefront of responsible gaming initiatives,” Jones asserted. Addabbo: Resorts World a ‘proven commodity’ While the CAC is still tasked with holding a vote on Resorts World’s application, that feels like a formality by now. If the vote is to reflect public support, speakers made a rejection all but impossible across both hearings. “Resorts World’s always been there for our community,” said state Senator Joe Addabbo, a prominent advocate of gambling legislation in New York. “So this is not a risk for this CAC to vote on, this is a proven commodity in Ozone Park. This is a proven commodity for our city, this is a proven commodity for our state.” Dozens upon dozens of community groups and nonprofits testified glowingly about Resorts World, with many acknowledging their initial skepticism when it first opened as a VLT facility. But 14 years of community efforts goes a long way, especially compared to the other bids. Most of those have been drumming up support only for the past three years or less. “They deserve a full licence, without a doubt, because they created the opportunity for gaming resources to be understood and appreciated by New Yorkers,” said state Senator Leroy Comrie. “It would be a travesty if the commission picks other people other than Resorts, who have set the standard.” As with Freedom Plaza, neither a vote date nor additional hearings for Resorts World NYC are currently scheduled.

author: JJPTR
body: GENTING TauRx / Alzheimer’s drug (mainly HMTM, formerly LMTX) has had a mixed journey. There are reasons to say it looks like a failure in some respects, but not a clear-cut one. I’ll summarize where things stand, what the problems are, and what might still make it worthwhile (if it ever gets through regulatory approval). What is it / Background TauRx Pharmaceuticals is a biotech company in which Genting Berhad holds about 20–21%. The drug is hydromethylthionine mesylate (HMTM), a tau aggregation inhibitor. Tau proteins are involved in Alzheimer's disease, so the idea is to slow down or stop disease progression by reducing tau aggregation. Earlier, it had LMTX (another formulation) in Phase 3 trials for Alzheimer’s and behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). Some of these trials failed to meet their co-primary endpoints. Evidence For Failure Here are the key criticisms / “failure‐like” outcomes: Primary endpoints not met Some of the Phase 3 trials (e.g. of LMTX) did not meet their co-primary endpoints. That means the trial’s main goals (cognitive, functional improvements, etc.) weren’t statistically satisfied when comparing the treatment group vs control/placebo. Problem with placebo / control groups In some cases, the control (placebo) or what was used was found to also have medical benefit (or what was thought to be placebo actually had some effect). That muddies the comparison, and reduces confidence in whether the experimental drug is truly better. Regulatory / investor skepticism Because of the above, there’s hesitance from regulators, analysts, and investors. People want more evidence, more robust trials, clearer endpoints. Previous trials failing Earlier LMTX studies (before the latest HMTM ones) had disappointing outcomes. That history makes people more cautious. Evidence for it Maybe Still Having Potential On the other hand, there are signs that it’s not totally dead: Some positive – post-hoc or subgroup analyses Even where primary endpoints were missed overall, in certain subgroups (e.g. people not taking other Alzheimer’s medications) there were signals of benefit. Also in early-stage disease, some improvements or slower decline are reported. Safety profile It is reported to have a relatively good safety track record (e.g. less risk of brain bleeding, which is a concern with some Alzheimer’s treatments) in some reports. Regulatory engagement is ongoing TauRx is still pushing for regulatory submissions (e.g. US, Canada, UK). And newer results (e.g. from the LUCIDITY trial) are being presented. If approved, it could still have commercial value. Cost and accessibility aspects One of the selling points is that HMTM is oral (vs many Alzheimer’s drugs which are injected or expensive monoclonal antibodies) and potentially much cheaper. If it works meaningfully, that could make a difference especially in wider populations. Where Things Probably Stand Now The fact that earlier primary endpoints were not met strongly suggests that the drug is not the breakthrough many hoped for. It may not deliver large, consistent effects across broad Alzheimer’s patient groups. Regulatory approval will be difficult: regulators tend to demand very robust, reproducible, statistically significant outcomes, especially for neurodegenerative diseases where many past drugs have failed. Even if it gets approved, its market would likely be limited to specific subgroups (e.g. early Alzheimer’s, patients not on certain other meds, etc.), not a panacea. My Take: Has It Failed? Not totally failed, but its prospects are much more modest than the hype might have suggested. It looks like it is not the sweeping Alzheimer’s cure people might have hoped for; rather, it might deliver something incremental (slowing progression under certain conditions) if the positive signals hold up. author: ImCK
body: GENS maintain is good already but if they still want see significant growth they need setup cruise port synergy with Resorts World cruises GENS is maintaining well, but if they want to achieve significant growth, they need to build cruise port synergy with Resorts World Cruises. By establishing a dedicated cruise port at Resorts World Sentosa, GENS can directly channel cruise passengers into the integrated resort. This creates a self-sustaining ecosystem where hotel rooms, attractions, F&B, and the casino benefit from a constant inflow of tourists. Each cruise ship carries up to 3,352 passengers, who, upon docking, are essentially “locked in” within Sentosa. With limited alternatives nearby, these visitors naturally spend their time and money within the RWS ecosystem — boosting yields across all business segments. In addition, RW Cruises can bundle its itineraries with island facilities such as Universal Studios Singapore and the SEA Aquarium, creating attractive package deals that enhance guest experience while maximizing spend. This direct-supply strategy transforms Resorts World Sentosa from a standalone IR into a controlled tourism hub, securing consistent volumes of international visitors. The synergy ensures a win-win model for both RWS and RW Cruises — and establishes a competitive advantage no rival can easily replicate.

author: ImCK
body: Currently, cruise passengers dock at Marina Bay Cruise Centre or HarbourFront (VivoCity). To reach Resorts World Sentosa, they must transfer via cable car, bus, or taxi — an inconvenient process that adds friction and reduces the conversion rate of cruise tourists into RWS visitors.

body: Genting’s operating profit in Singapore declined amid higher costs from ongoing brownfield construction, and the temporary closure of SEA Aquarium in May and June this year to facilitate the opening of the Singapore Oceanarium. In Las Vegas, Genting was affected by lower visitor volume that dragged on its hotels and gaming revenue amid macroeconomic uncertainty. Genting has submitted a formal bid for a casino licence in New York, as part of a US$5.5 billion (RM23.16 billion) resort development in Queens. A decision is expected by Dec 1, a key outcome for Genting, S&P noted. “If awarded, the level of investment and incremental earnings from the new licence will be the main rating considerations, and we believe Genting will continue with similar financial policy settings,” the ratings agency said. In contrast, the agency warned that a failed bid could weigh on the competitiveness of Genting’s US operations, though it would remove the overhang of the cost of investing in new business. “Our base-case assumptions do not reflect investments or incremental earnings related to the group bidding for the New York gaming licence, as we view it as an event risk,” S&P added.

Resorts World, which currently operates as a "racino" offering electronic gambling machines but no live table games, has been operating in South Ozone Park for almost 15 years since opening at the Aqueduct Race Track in 2011. It has long been one of the favorites to obtain one of the three licenses set to be awarded by the State Gaming Commission this December due to the infrastructure already in place at the site. The proposal became only the second project to earn CAC approval after MGM Empire City, another racino located in Yonkers, received unanimous approval Thursday morning. author: ImCK
body: Nevada’s high-end gaming salons could get more exposure and more players if the Nevada Gaming Commission approves amendments to a regulation to be considered Thursday. Gaming salons are special rooms in which high rollers and celebrities can gamble out of public view. Most high-end casinos have them and offer play in them to big spenders, entertainers and professional athletes who don’t want to see pictures of themselves spread on social media. Among the Nevada casinos with salons are Wynn and Encore Las Vegas, Bellagio, The Venetian and The Palazzo, Resorts World Las Vegas, Durango and Reno’s Grand Sierra Resort. Nevada law says licensed operators must open their casinos to the public without an admission charge. But in 2001, the Nevada Legislature allowed for the establishment of salons with special rules to insure privacy to players. In December, several resorts approached gaming regulators about amending the salon rules to encourage more play. Some of the changes presented by the Nevada Resort Association required legislative action and Senate Bill 459 was unanimously approved by the state Senate and Assembly in May. The Nevada Gaming Control Board conducted a workshop meeting in August to discuss prospective changes. The Control Board recommended approving amended regulation on Sept. 10, setting the stage for final approval by the Gaming Commission. The changes in the regulation include: — The financial criteria for admission into a gaming salon would be reduced from $300,000. When salons were initially introduced, the financial threshold was $500,000. In 2008, regulators reduced that amount to $300,000. The Resort Association suggested that amounts be determined by individual properties, but the new amended threshold under consideration is $20,000. Get updates from the editors of GMToday.com sent directly to your email inbox: — Poker would be added to the list of games offered in salons. The regulation would require an individual player buy-in of $10,000 with a total $20,000 staked for a game to be conducted. -Salon slot machine minimums would be at the discretion of the licensee. That’s similar to existing rules allowing licensees to determine minimums for salon table games. Originally, slot machine minimums were included in legislation and set at $500, but the Legislature approved the modification. — Casinos would be allowed to convert private salons to public gaming without prior written approval from the Control Board chairman. The amendments would also enable a guest of a casino patron qualified for salon play to stay up to 24 hours instead of six hours currently allowed. Attracting more players Board members believe the modified rules would enable casinos to attract more high-end players to use salons and generate more revenue for the companies and in taxes. “What’s interesting about this is that the goals actually remain the same, bringing more revenue to the state of Nevada in an economic uncertain time and allowing for a flexible and unique amenity that certain nonrestricted licensees can offer their valued patrons,” Control Board Chairman Mike Dreitzer said in the September board meeting. Dreitzer said the Legislature’s passage of Senate Bill 459 set the stage for the regulatory changes under consideration. “The task here before us is to adopt revised regulations consistent with the statutory change, done in such a way that is reasonable and consistent with good regulatory oversight,” he said, “while at the same time supporting Nevada’s licensees and their desire to utilize this important economic tool to produce greater revenue all in the face of ever growing competition across the world and certainly across the U.S.”

body: The real story behind the slump in Las Vegas tourism September 26, 2025 Here's a summary of the key points and analysis: Core Issue: The Las Vegas Tourism Slump The segment explores a sharp decline in Las Vegas tourism, marked by: · 12% drop in visitation (year-over-year for July 2025). · Decreased hotel occupancy, airport traffic, and vehicle traffic from California. · Layoffs and reduced hours for hospitality workers (e.g., Larry Turner, a casino porter, noting how much quieter it is). Proposed Causes: A Multi-Faceted Problem The discussion identifies several interconnected reasons for the slump: 1. Economic Factors & "The Hangover": · Post-Boom Correction: Analyst Jeremy Aguero suggests the slump is partly a correction from an unsustainable "sugar high" in 2023-2024, driven by major events like the Super Bowl and Formula One, and post-COVID stimulus spending. · Consumer Sentiment: Aguero highlights a national drop in consumer confidence and high household debt, making discretionary travel spending one of the first things people cut. · High Costs: A major theme is that Las Vegas is perceived as becoming too expensive. Guests and social media users complain about high resort fees, parking costs, $30 cocktails, and room rates, leading to a feeling of being "ripped off." 2. Political Factors & The "Trump Slump": · Commissioner Tick Segerblom and Culinary Union President Diana Valles directly blame the Trump administration's policies. · They cite a significant drop in international tourists, particularly from Canada and Mexico (the top two sources), attributing it to inflammatory rhetoric and policies that make visitors feel "unwelcome." · They also note fear and stress within the immigrant-heavy workforce. 3. Structural Industry Issues: · Price Gouging vs. Cost Drivers: There's a debate about the root of high prices. Reasons include inflation, high labor costs (after significant union wage increases), and upkeep of massive resorts. However, there's also an acknowledgment that corporations may have pushed prices beyond consumer tolerance. · Loss of Value Messaging: Plaza Hotel CEO Jonathan Jossel suggests Vegas forgot it's not just an "event town" and needs to recapture its image as a place for an affordable, fun weekend. Las Vegas as a Bellwether The segment positions Las Vegas as a "canary in the coal mine" for the U.S. economy. Its heavy reliance on discretionary spending makes it particularly sensitive to shifts in national economic confidence and consumer wallets. Resilience and Adaptation Despite the slump, there is optimism about Vegas's ability to adapt: · Historical Resilience: The city has bounced back from major shocks like 9/11 and COVID-19. · Market Corrections: The industry is already responding with city-wide sales, discounted rooms, and all-inclusive packages to address cost concerns. MGM Resorts' CEO admitted they "let the narrative get away" and are emphasizing value. · Constant Reinvention: The city has a long history of transforming itself, from the Rat Pack era to becoming a sports and spectacle hub (e.g., The Sphere). Conclusion The segment concludes that the slump is likely a combination of a natural economic correction, specific national policies affecting international travel, and self-inflicted wounds related to pricing. The future depends on the industry's ability to restore a sense of value and "return on experience" while navigating a less confident national economic climate.

body: 最佳时机：为何是2026年？ 这是一个战略性的时间窗口，旨在将以下几个潜在利好资本化： · 纽约赌牌效应： 假设成功中标，完整的赌牌将为RWNYC带来质的飞跃，其盈利预期将达到顶峰，成为IPO故事中最亮眼的部分。 · 业绩验证期： 到2026年，RWLV将有足够的时间来证明其已实现稳定盈利，能够提供扎实的财务数据来支撑估值。 · 周期把握： 云顶可以主动选择在预计的市场繁荣周期中进行操作，以最大化募资效果。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 此项计划堪称云顶美国战略的“终局之战”，但其成功依赖于三大支柱的稳固： 1. 纽约赌牌: · 没有这张牌，RWNYC就只是一个普通的VLT设施，其增长想象空间有限，整个IPO故事的吸引力将大幅下降。 2. 盈利能力: · RWLV必须彻底摆脱“拖累”的标签，展现出强劲且持续的现金流生成能力。RWNYC在获得赌牌后也需要展现出明确的盈利增长轨迹。 3. 市场环境...不可或缺的“东风” · 一个健康、活跃的资本市场是大型IPO成功的温床。若届时处于熊市或利率高企，投资者会对高风险的增长型故事失去兴趣。

body: As of late September 2025, three bids for a New York City-area casino license have advanced past the initial community approval stage, with the state expected to award the licenses by the end of the year. The three successful bids include expansions of existing facilities in Queens and Yonkers, as well as a new development in the Bronx. Other proposals in Manhattan and Brooklyn have been rejected. Bids that advanced - 1) MGM Empire City (Yonkers): This proposal expands an existing "racino" (a facility with video lottery terminals) into a full-scale casino with live table games. 2) Resorts World New York City (Queens): This bid plans to convert the existing racino at Aqueduct Racetrack into a full-fledged casino. 3) Bally's Bronx: This plan proposes a new casino at the Ferry Point public golf course in the Bronx and was approved by its Community Advisory Committee (CAC) in late September 2025.

body: Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) Rationale: trophy Strip asset but use conservative discount to replacement cost. Conservative range: USD 0.30b – 0.40b (USD 300–400m) Conservative midpoint: USD 0.35b Resorts World Bimini (Bahamas) Rationale: small island resort, seasonal demand, thin liquidity. author: KooSan
body: When lecanemab and donanemab, two drugs targeting another protein beta-amyloid, were approved by America’s Food and Drug Administration, it seemed like a huge moment in the battle against Alzheimer’s. But sceptics said the drugs produced only minimal improvements in early-stage dementia while having extremely dangerous side-effects, causing brain bleeds which proved fatal for at least two people during trials. The two drugs, which have to be delivered by intravenous infusion, are also. extremely expensive. That led NICE, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, to rule that they should not be prescribed in the NHS because they were not cost-effective. By contrast, TauRx’s medical director Dr Sonya Miller, insists its drug, taken as a tablet, is free of serious side effects and affordable. “We've got what we believe is safe and effective oral treatment here for Alzheimer's. This really is a world first.”

author: KooSan
body: So, what is this whole placebo kencing issue and CPAD. Most of us are in the dark. There are two massive hurdles to clear. A paper on the phase 3 clinical trial of HMTM has been submitted for publication in a leading medical journal and the UK medicines regulator the MHRA is considering whether to approve the drug. The journal will now be seeking the views of eminent scientists in the Alzheimer’s field, and if they are not impressed then it is very unlikely that the MHRA will be either. You see, Taurx failed to hit one clinical endpoint, a self-imposed target. Lucidity needed to show an appreciably better outcome after 12 months for participants given HMTM compared to those given a placebo, and it missed the mark. Both sets of patients saw the progression of their Alzheimer’s slow down but there was not a big enough gap between those on the drug and those given the placebo. There was however an oddity about the placebo which TauRx believes puts things in a better light. HMTM has a curious but harmless side-effect in that about half of those who take it see their kencing change colour. At an early,stage of the drug’s development it went a bright blue, now it has amore restrained but still noticeable greenish tinge. Now, the rules for a classic double blind clinical trial are strict - the participants in such a trial must not be given any clue as to whether they are getting the drug or a placebo. But if they learned about this urine side-effect and saw that it was absent in their case, participants might decide to drop out of the trial. So a team of chemists at Aberdeen University was set a difficult challenge - find a way of making a placebo which turns kencing green. Try as they might, they could not find a way of doing this safely so eventually TauRx came up with a rather unsatisfactory solution - they spiked the placebo with a tiny amount of the drug. This had the desired effect but, even this very low dose of HMTM had a positive impact on those given the placebo. It was not a dramatic difference but enough to narrow the gap after a year with the results for those receiving the full dose of the drug to such an extent that the target was missed. The MHRA may nevertheless not look kindly on a trial which by one important measure has failed but TauRx has a plan to allay the regulator’s fears - by effectively recruiting another set of trial participants given a pure placebo. For this they turned to CPAD, the US Critical Path for Alzheimer’s Disease, a database containing the records of thousands of people with Alzheimer’s who have taken part in previous clinical trials. They selected a group of people, who had received a placebo and were as closely matched as possible to those on the Lucidity trial given the drug, and compared their outcomes after 18 months. The results showed a 35% reduction in brain shrinkage for Lucidity patients compared to the CPAD placebo group, and on two cognition tests the group on the drug saw their results decline around 80% less than those given a sugar pill. If TauRx is to be believed its phase 3 results, apart from that little spiked placebo problem, are of a different order, providing compelling evidence of a safe and effective drug. If the company is painting an accurate picture, one would hope that the MHRA could be lenient about what feels like a minor error in the trial process and NICE could then move swiftly to allow the NHS to prescribe HMTM.

body: 🧩 Context: Why LVS, WYNN & MGM dropped and how this benefit GENTING The sell-off on Friday wasn’t because the global casino industry is collapsing — it was Macau-specific and sentiment-driven: • Weak Golden Week travel numbers from China → lower Macau gaming expectations. • Weather disruption / storm risk → short-term revenue hit. • Investor risk rotation out of “China exposure.” So, the issue is mostly Macau and Chinese tourism, not the U.S. or ASEAN casino market. 💡 Short-Term Effects (Next Few Weeks) ✅ Investor Rotation Benefit • U.S. and ASEAN investors may rotate out of Macau-heavy stocks (LVS, WYNN, MGM) into non-Macau operators like Genting Singapore and Genting Malaysia. • Fund managers seeking exposure to gaming recovery but wanting to avoid China risk will find Genting relatively safer. ✅ RWLV (Las Vegas) • RWLV could actually benefit from this shift • U.S. leisure spending remains resilient. • Las Vegas strip demand stable → U.S. gaming earnings viewed as “safe cash flow.” • Some funds that trim LVS, MGM positions could rotate part of that capital into RWLV’s parent exposure via Genting Berhad. ✅ Valuation Multiple Gap May Narrow • Genting stocks have been trading at a “conglomerate discount” • If Macau sentiment stays weak, Genting’s diversified earnings become more attractive → valuation uplift potential. 🔮 4️⃣ Medium-Term Effects (2–6 Months) • RWNY & NY Casino License Story Strengthens: • With MGM distracted by weak Macau sentiment, Genting’s RWNY license narrative becomes even more strategic — investors see it as growth anchored in the U.S., not in China. • This can support Genting Berhad and GENM share price ahead of the license decision. • GENS (Singapore) Stability Premium: • Singapore tourism continues to recover steadily from ASEAN and India, not just China. • GENS often rallies when Macau weakens because it captures “safe Asia gaming” flows. ⚖️ 5️⃣ Net Impact Summary Time Horizon Genting Berhad Genting Malaysia Genting Singapore Short Term (1–3 weeks) Slight upside from rotation Stable, potential upside Likely outperform regionally Medium Term (3–6 months) Moderate upside if NY license news improves Strong upside (Empire Resort story) Defensive outperformance. US Assets consolidation and listing separately in NYSE? 🧭 In summary: • LVS, WYNN & MGM declines are negative for Macau sentiment, but positive for Genting’s relative positioning. • Genting’s U.S. and Singapore diversification now look more valuable. • Expect fund inflows and a potential relative outperformance window over the next 4–8 weeks.

body: let me summary how the sell and lease stragegy impact for you your question is putting other factor in but ignoring other impact . when you talk about leasing you should think about how they use the money after sell the money is die de meh put in FD earn interest / settle finance cost . Sullivan County Development & Empire Resorts Restructuring Impact Summary Under the proposed structure, Sullivan County Development (SCD) will acquire the non-gaming assets (such as land, buildings, or other property) currently owned by Empire Resorts (Empire). Empire will then use the sale proceeds to settle its financing obligations and subsequently lease back the land and facilities from SCD. This arrangement effectively transforms Empire into an asset-light operator and delivers multiple positive financial and operational impacts: Finance Cost Eliminated – The sale proceeds allow Empire to settle outstanding loans, thereby removing high finance costs and improving net profitability and cash flow. Lower Lease Expense – By leasing the assets back from a county-controlled entity (SCD), Empire can regain operational control at a lower rental rate, reducing its ongoing lease burden. Additional Management Revenue – Empire can enter into a management or operations agreement with SCD, earning management fees that create a new and stable revenue stream. Depreciation Reduction – The transfer of large property, plant, and equipment (PPE) to SCD removes significant depreciation expenses from Empire’s books, improving its EBITDA margin and overall earnings quality. No More Facility Upkeep Costs – With SCD owning the property, all future maintenance, capital improvements, and property-related taxes are handled by SCD. This lowers Empire’s fixed operating cost base and enhances flexibility. Overall Impact: The transaction strengthens Empire’s balance sheet, eliminates heavy finance and depreciation burdens, reduces leasing and upkeep costs, and introduces new management income. This asset-light transformation improves profitability, cash flow stability, and long-term competitiveness while maintaining control over core gaming operations.

author: BeCoolFST
body: @Lim, fair point on the economic opportunity. We are moving into a more constructive discussion. However, from the perspective of government agency/enity, they don't necessarily take only economic stand, they also consider society wellbeing and job creation opportunity at the expense of pure economic gain. The role of government is not to make business, rather is to create a conducive environment for bussiness and job-creation to thrive. In addition, government entity also often consider a much longer time horizon than business entity. When Sullivan country decides to take over the non-gaming assets, they must have considered the number of job opportunity they can provide themselves, the long term dividend that the business will provide well beyond the usual business projections. Government may also consider the opportunity to create jobs as being more attractive than the gain made by this single business transaction. The wages paid for all the job created can have more multiplier economic effects

author: magellan
body: September 25, 2025 US500+++M Casino Rescue Plan Hinges on Boom. Analysts Predict Bust. Sullivan County (SC) tells investors there will be massive growth at a Catskills casino resort, but its own consultants predict decline. Sullivan County (SC) asks investors to ​lend ​more than USD500M to rescue struggling Resorts World Catskills​, predicting that casino resort will soon be flooded with visitors and make dramatically more money — even though its own consultants predict the opposite.

author: magellan
body: Hear SC's pitch. Investors would buy up to $585M bonds from SC’s newly-formed local dev corp., spun out of its Industrial Development Agency, or IDA. The corp. would buy 2 hotels, golf course, and event venue — almost everything except casino itself — from current owner, Empire Resorts, Inc. The cash infusion could enable Empire Resorts to invest in the property and to pay off $300M in debt due next year, helping it stave off possible bankruptcy.

author: magellan
body: The non-casino properties, the dev corp. assures investors, will soon become a cash cow. Because parent co. of Empire Resorts (ER) is a heavy favorite to win a casino license in Queens, the corporation reasons, Empire Resorts (ER) will soon have a database with a 1M new table game customers. It will be able to entice some to travel to Catskills, with its lower gaming tax rates, and to stay in resort. By 2029, hotel room occupancy will increase nearly 16%, non-gaming revenue will climb a whopping 80%, and investors will make a tidy profit. The problem? Two studies prepared for the county came to very different conclusions. Local and county officials have long predicted that three new downstate casinos will draw customers away from Resorts World Catskill, as a New York source reported in 2023, and analysts have agreed. Consulting firm C&W prepared an appraisal of non-gaming assets which forecasted that Catskills hotel occupancy will drop to 60 % by 2029, rather than rising to the 86.5 % predicted in the bond pitch. (> The C&W analysis is attached to the investor pitch, which does not explain the contradictory findings. C&W was retained by the firm the dev corp. picked to underwrite the bond offering. <)

author: magellan
body: Another firm, CC prepared a separate analysis for the county finding downstate casinos could cause Resorts World Catskills (RWC) revenue to plummet up to 76 % and negatively impact tax revenues from related businesses — such as the resort’s hotels. Yet the investor pitch predicted an 80 % revenue increase for those businesses by 2029. The IDA’s executive director, Jennifer Flad, declined to explain these discrepancies. “I am not in a position to respond to some of your questions,” she wrote. So what happens if the corporation can’t pay investors back

author: magellan
body: Proposed bond offering stipulates taxpayers aren’t on the hook for investor losses. Matt McPhillips, chair of SC Legislature’s economic development committee, told Radio Catskill that taxpayers “have no stake in this deal.” “There’s no collateral that the county or its taxpayers are responsible for,” McPhillips said. “This is more to allow the casino to reconsolidate, reposition itself, and really invest in this property.” But at the request of interested buyers, the local dev corp. recently brought in lawyers to analyze ways to protect investors in case of default.

author: magellan
body: A default could create political pressure for the state or county to intervene. Resorts World Casino plays a major role in the local economy and employs over a 1,000 people, its developers received more than $50 million in local tax breaks, and it regularly asks Albany for deeper subsidies. A default could also harm the county’s reputation and increase its future borrowing costs, according to David Brittenham, a SC resident and retired partner at a major law firm whose practice focused on corporate financing deals. “A default could potentially be taken into account by credit agencies in evaluating the county itself — and its borrowing capacity,” Brittenham said. “It’s at least going to be a black eye.” It’s not clear whether Sullivan County (SC) consulted independent bond ratings agencies, such as Fitch, Moody’s, or Standard & Poor’s, about the implications of a default for the county. No rating agency has given the investment opportunity a formal grade.

author: magellan
body: Brittenham said allowing Empire Resorts to go into bankruptcy could have been a better path for SC — and wouldn’t necessarily have involved layoffs. “It’s not clear to me they got expert investment banking advice about their options,” he said. “Bankruptcy, to me, should have been evaluated seriously, because under our bankruptcy law, the idea is to rehabilitate the business, not simply to wind it up. And there are plenty of companies that go through bankruptcy, sometimes more than once, with little or no loss of jobs.” The county was shaken by the shuttering of a Frito-Lay plant in Liberty this spring that cost nearly 300 jobs. It’s not clear whether Resorts World threatened layoffs, prompting the county’s $585M venture. A company spokesperson did not respond to questions. The undertaking has played out almost entirely behind closed doors; McPhillips, the county legislator, did not respond to questions either. The bailout isn’t yet a done deal, and the formal bond offering continues to face delays.

body: 讨论得很精彩，这个观点确实有一定道理。 目前美国和欧洲确实在加速去风险化de-risking，要摆脱对中国供应链的依赖。 例如美国的CHIPS法案 和通胀削减法案，欧洲的关键原材料法案，都在重建本地制造与战略供应链，从全球化转向盟友化。 短期来看，中国出口仍强劲，属于“短赢”； 但长期而言，西方市场收紧、关税上升、供应链重组，确实会让中国外贸承压。 尤其当中国商品转向亚洲市场时，价格竞争加剧，东南亚国家可能首当其冲，制造业利润被挤压，甚至出现更多贷款违约风险。 不过，也不能过度悲观。 西方的内部重建会推高成本与通胀，不一定全面带动经济繁荣； 中国自身也在推双循环，强化内需与科技创新，适应能力仍然强。 而亚洲中部分国家如越南、印度、马来西亚...反而可能因供应链转移而受惠。

body: 从经济学角度来看，这种现象其实并不一定是坏事。 当市场上竞争者太多时，就会出现恶性竞争、价格战等情况。结果是...谁的成本更低，谁才能生存下来；成本高、效率低的公司最终会被淘汰出局。 随着市场参与者逐渐减少，供需重新平衡，价格也会自然回升。此时，幸存下来的企业利润开始恢复，吸引新的公司再次进入市场。 这就是典型的market cleansing mechanism 也是经济周期的一部分。 简单来说..市场通过竞争不断自我修正

The reason is because GENT would have negotiated the price with substantial shareholders of GENM. Including these two groups, GENM would cease to satisfy the 25% minimum share needed to be floated in public to be considered as a listed company. author: Michaelchan2024
body: The main purpose of Genting Berhad’s move to privatize GenM and consolidate Empire Resorts is financial and strategic, not merely about cutting headcount or trimming payroll. 1. Debt Restructuring By combining GenM and Empire Resorts’ debt under Genting Berhad, the group can reduce its overall credit risk and lower financing costs. Genting Berhad’s stronger balance sheet and higher credit standing allow it to secure better borrowing terms and manage liabilities more efficiently. 2. Corporate Simplification This move streamlines the entire corporate structure, removing inter-company complexities and overlapping ownership layers. A cleaner structure enhances transparency, improves management efficiency, and positions the group more favorably for a potential U.S. listing or future fundraising exercise. 3. Operational Synergy With all major assets under one roof, Genting can align its strategic direction across Malaysia, the U.S., and Singapore without internal friction. This unified control enables faster decisionmaking, resource optimization, and a clearer global growth strategy.

author: Joe18
body: Key Takeaways on Genting's Leverage: ​Debt-to-Equity: At 73.6% to 77%, Genting Berhad's Debt-to-Equity is relatively moderate for a capital-intensive casino and leisure group, and is significantly lower than some of the highly-leveraged US and Macau operators. ​Debt-to-EBITDA: The Debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 5x to 6.5x places it within the range often considered typical or slightly on the higher end for major global casino companies. The high capital expenditures and asset-heavy nature of the casino business inherently lead to higher leverage ratios in this sector. ​The Genting Group is a conglomerate: The Genting parent company figure is a consolidated number. Its different listed entities, such as Genting Singapore (GUTS), are reported as having very little debt (near 0% Debt-to-Equity), while Genting Malaysia (GENM) has higher leverage (around 120% Debt-to-Equity).

author: ImCK
body: As for RWC, it will benefit as RWNYC will direct comps to be redeemed there. RWNYC’s business model is to provide players generating the top 30 percent GGR with 20 percent complimentary expenses. This amounts to between $140 to $200 million a year, and RWNYC will direct up to 50 percent—to be redeemed at RWC. Because players typically spend at least $2 for every $1 of complimentary value, this initiative is expected to generate an additional $140 to $200 million in incremental revenue for RWC, nearly doubling its current revenues and resulting in a strong and sustainable Catskills operation. This arrangement is mutually beneficial, as players in RWNYC will value the offers to vacation at RWC, such as playing at the Monster golf course and visiting Sullivan County’s attractions. RWNYC is the only operator among the finalists that will not divert its New York-based players to lower-tax jurisdictions such as Atlantic City. Instead, RWNYC will direct half its loyalty rewards to RWC and, if necessary, to RWHV should MGM be granted a License — thereby keeping all gaming spending within the State. RWNYC is the only proposal that will not cannibalize RWC and RWHV and maximize long-term economic benefits for all of New York, without leakage to other States.

author: Linewalker95
body: Let's calculate this step-by-step. We know from the original announcement: GENT's initial stake: 49.36% Total number of GENM shares: 2.87 billion shares / 50.64% (the portion they don't own). This means the total issued shares of GENM = 2.87 billion / 0.5064 = **approximately **5.667 billion shares****. From the new announcement on 14 Oct 2025: GENT bought an additional 9,000,000 shares. 1. Calculate New Number of Shares Held First, find the initial number of shares GENT held: Initial Shares Held = 49.36% of 5.667 billion = 0.4936 * 5,667,000,000 = 2,796,000,000 shares (approximately). Now add the new shares they bought: New Total Shares Held = 2,796,000,000 + 9,000,000 = 2,805,000,000 shares. 2. Calculate New Percentage New Percentage = (New Total Shares Held / Total Issued Shares) * 100 = (2,805,000,000 / 5,667,000,000) * 100 = 49.49%.

author: hw0706
body: First, the applicant will have to put down a deposit into the state’s coffers — the exact amount to be determined by the state commission — of no less than 5% and no more than 10% of the project’s total investment. That’s just a part of a lot more money the license winners will owe the state, because whoever wins one of the coveted casino licenses has to pay the state $500 million for it. They also have to spend a minimum of $500 million in “capital investments” in the area where they will be located, which could mean anything from building subsidized housing to contributing to local transit improvements or creating public park space. Licensees will also have to answer all requests from the state for information, register its new employees and complete steps to maintain certificates to open to the public. In addition, the revenue from future gaming will be taxed at a not-yet-determined rate that the gaming board has said will be at least 25% for slot gaming and at least 10% for all other gaming revenue. According to City Limits, when the state legislature was considering the change, Spectrum Gaming — hired by the state’s gaming board to crunch the numbers on expanding casino downstate — said new gaming facilities in the New York City area would produce $5.5 billion in gross gambling revenue, $841 million a year in tax revenue and create 30,000 jobs in New York. According to the three proposals on the table now, the developers say that, together, the projects could create close to 15,500 permanent jobs and around 75,500 indirect and direct construction jobs. But in a 2023 analysis of the impact of expanding gambling facilities in upstate New York — approved several years earlier — revenue results were a mixed bag. The state comptroller found that though those casinos brought in $176 million for local governments between 2017 and 2022, they did fail to meet their initial revenue and tax projections during that same time period. “Local gaming revenue is not always a ‘sure bet,’” the report noted. “Careful financial planning is crucial to minimize risk while benefiting from this revenue stream.”

author: hw0706
body: Moody’s Ratings has placed the issuer ratings of Genting Berhad, Genting Overseas Holdings Limited, and Genting Singapore Limited under review for downgrade, warning that Genting Berhad’s proposed acquisition of the remaining shares in Genting Malaysia Berhad could significantly strain the group’s financial strength. The review affects Genting Berhad’s Baa2 issuer rating, Genting Overseas Holdings’ Baa2 issuer rating, and Genting Singapore’s A3 issuer rating, all of which previously carried a stable outlook. Moody’s also placed on review the Baa2 backed senior unsecured rating of the notes issued by Genting Overseas Holdings’ subsidiary, GOHL Capital Limited. The credit review follows Genting Berhad’s announcement of a conditional voluntary cash offer of MYR2.35 ($0.49) per share to acquire the remaining 50.6 percent of Genting Malaysia it does not already own. The deal, valued at up to MYR6.74 billion ($1.6 billion), would be largely funded by as much as MYR6.3 billion ($1.5 billion) in new debt and is expected to close within 60 days, subject to regulatory approval and shareholder acceptance. “The review for downgrade reflects our expectation that Genting Berhad’s credit quality will weaken materially, depending on the level of acceptance of its proposed takeover offer for Genting Malaysia, which will be largely debt-funded,” said Anthony Prayugo, a Moody’s Ratings Analyst. “Genting Berhad’s credit metrics are already weak and the proposed transaction would delay any meaningful deleveraging.” Moody’s estimates that Genting Berhad’s adjusted debt-to-EBITDA ratio could rise to about 5.1 times in 2025 if the acquisition is completed as planned, surpassing its 4.0x downgrade threshold. The agency previously expected Genting to improve its leverage through earnings growth from its gaming operations in Malaysia, Singapore, and Las Vegas, but now anticipates that the new debt will postpone recovery. The agency also noted that Genting Berhad’s financial profile could deteriorate further if its subsidiary Genting New York LLC succeeds in winning one of three casino licenses in downstate New York, which could entail $5.5 billion in potential investment. Despite the added risk, Moody’s said Genting Berhad maintains strong liquidity, supported by dividends from its operating subsidiaries and a well-managed debt maturity profile. The review is expected to conclude within 60–90 days and will assess the transaction’s final funding structure and the group’s plans to reduce leverage. Genting Overseas Holdings’ and Genting Singapore’s ratings are being reviewed in line with the parent company’s downgrade watch. Moody’s emphasized that Genting Singapore’s standalone financial strength remains solid, underpinned by minimal debt and substantial cash holdings of SG$3.3 billion ($2.43 billion) as of June 2025.

author: Joe18
body: For a hotel or casino, ADR stands for Average Daily Rate, which is the average revenue earned per occupied room for a specific period. It is calculated by dividing the total room revenue by the total number of rooms sold and is a key performance indicator for measuring a property's financial health and room pricing strategy. How to calculate ADR Formula: ADR = Total Room Revenue / Total Number of Rooms Sold Example: If a hotel earns $10,000 in room revenue by selling 100 rooms, the ADR is $100 ($10,000 / 100). What ADR indicates Performance: It helps measure the average price point at which rooms are being sold. Financial health: A higher ADR can indicate greater profitability from each occupied room. Pricing strategy: By tracking ADR, managers can see if their pricing is effective and where it can be improved through strategies like upselling or adjusting prices based on demand. Competitor analysis: ADR can be used to compare a property's performance against its competitors.

author: cktay
body: So much talk of Genting taking GENM 100% private (for a whooping RM6.74billion) Ask yourself why the need to do so --- taking 100% private? Any benefits? More likely it is just the intention to bring its share above 50% When a company owns over 50% of another, it typically uses consolidation accounting, treating both entities as a single economic unit and combining their financial statements. The parent company combines 100% of the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses into its own financial statements but the minority interests will also be accounted for on the parent's financial statements. It also triggers mandatory disclosure and ? a compulsory acquisition process for the remaining minority shares. So is there really an intention to take GENM private in the first place. Why wasn’t it done around the lows of RM1.46 when GENM’s shareholders were panicking and more likely to sell for a premium of 2.35-1.46 = 89s.

author: riko
body: ikan bilis like to talk 3 talk 4 ... -_- An ADR, or American Depositary Receipt, is a certificate issued by a US bank that represents shares of a foreign company. It allows US investors to buy stock in overseas companies through US stock exchanges, in US dollars, without the hassle of trading on foreign markets or dealing with foreign currency. Each ADR can represent one or more shares of the foreign stock. Yes, an increase in an ADR's price generally means the underlying foreign shares are also increasing, since the ADR's price is directly tied to the foreign stock's value. An ADR is a certificate representing shares of a foreign company, and it trades on U.S. stock exchanges. Therefore, when an ADR's price goes up, it indicates the foreign shares it represents are likely rising in value in their home market, according to information from Charles Schwab and Robinhood

author: hw0706
body: If Genting Crosses 50% But Not 90% The takeover becomes unconditional (successful), so all acceptances are paid at RM 2.35 per share. Genting Berhad then owns, say, 60–75% of GENM — gaining majority control but not full ownership. GENM remains listed on Bursa Malaysia, because Genting’s stake is below 90%, and Public shareholding spread (≥ 25%) is likely still satisfied. However, with > 50% control, Genting effectively runs GENM with minimal interference from minorities.

author: Junkit Ng
body: BeCoolFST- its actually a common phenomenon that happens during a solo acquasition/ merger, they announce a buy out price then the stock will trade at that range in the secondary market during the entire buyout period. The reason for this phenomenon is cuz retail are betting that the buy out will be sucessful and they wanna offload at it at 2.35 without having to wait for LKT to send u a email and you sign it and wait X working days. In this senario retail flood the secondary market with their ASK at a cheaper price hoping other buyers will cash them out near LKT offer of 2.35. Now on the reason why LKT buying up all the 2.34 is a bad move is simple if he does he would destroy the retails ask wall of 2.33-2.34 which protects his offer of 2.35 if the stock is trading at 2.35 it could easily breach 2.36 and more out bidding LKT offer of 2.35. End of the day, the 2.33 2.34 you see the stock trading isnt really for LKT, its trading between stock holders. LKT has only started a notice of voluntary buy out, he havent started the process of said buy out (get email/ notice from bursa and sign/ confirm if u agree). That recent 1% buy he did is just to boost the company holding to more than 50% making it financially illogical for institution to fight his bid.

author: cktay
body: Published on 22 Oct 2025. RAM Ratings has affirmed the AA1/Stable/P1 corporate credit ratings of Genting Berhad (Genting or the Group) and Genting Malaysia Berhad (GenM) as well as the issue ratings of their debt programmes (Table 1). GenM’s ratings reflect close operational integration with Genting and our expectation of a ‘very high’ likelihood of parental financial support if needed. The ratings consider Genting’s robust business profile, underpinned by its diversified and leading gaming and leisure market footprint in Malaysia, Singapore and a prominent presence in the northeastern US video gaming machine market. The Group’s operations in plantations, power generation, property and oil and gas mitigate some degree of sector concentration risk. In our review, we have assessed the impact of potential material financial outlays for the proposed privatisation of GenM. In our view, a full privatisation of GenM is unlikely at the current offer price. Assuming a more moderate take up rate for this debt-funded privatisation, coupled with other planned capex and investments, our projections indicate the Group’s net debts to rise above RM27 bil in the period up to fiscal 2027. This would result in net gearing ratios exceeding 0.50 times while its funds from operations (FFO) net debt coverage may dip below 0.35 times, over the next three years. At these levels, Genting’s debt metrics would be strained but still within the tolerance limit of its current rating.

body: Is RAM is top international credit rating agency? ------ No — RAM Ratings (Rating Agency Malaysia Berhad) is not considered a top international credit rating agency. Here’s the breakdown 👇 🏦 What RAM Is RAM Ratings is a Malaysia-based domestic credit rating agency, established in 1990. It primarily rates Malaysian and some regional (ASEAN) corporate bonds, sukuk (Islamic debt), and structured finance instruments. It is recognized by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Securities Commission Malaysia, but not recognized globally as a Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organization (NRSRO) by the U.S. SEC. 🌍 Top International Rating Agencies These are the only agencies globally considered the “Big Three” international credit rating agencies: 1. Moody’s Investors Service (U.S.) 2. S&P Global Ratings (U.S.) 3. Fitch Ratings (U.K./U.S.) ✅ Their ratings are accepted globally for international bond issuance, cross-border investment benchmarks, and regulatory capital requirements

author: Michaelchan2024
body: Genting Berhad’s 77% debt to equity ratio stand out as the most conservative and financially sound among global peers. While US operators like Caesars, MGM, and Wynn operate under heavy leverage, Genting maintains ample liquidity and lower gearing, giving it greater resilience in a high interest or volatile market environment. Even with a total debt of RM65B, Genting’s strong cash position and diversified global operations should keep its debt to equity ratio manageable.

author: Dehcomic01
body: Genting’s Big Move: Will the VTO Fix a Low-Return Giant? Genting has been in the news recently with its voluntary takeover (VTO) proposal to acquire the remaining 51% of Genting Malaysia Berhad that it does not already own. In my article written before this announcement, I raised concerns about Genting’s weak ROIC, weighed down by a high fixed-cost base. I viewed Genting more as a defensive cash generator than a true growth compounder. The VTO signals strategic intent — to unlock better capital allocation, simplify the group structure, and pursue big-ticket ambitions such as potential U.S. expansion. The move does not change Genting’s underlying operational and efficiency challenges; those remain the key hurdles to long-term value creation. The weakness lies in capital efficiency — ROIC has rarely cleared 7%. EPS has shrunk over the past decade, and large expansions like Resorts World Las Vegas have lifted fixed costs without delivering matching returns. Unlocking value depends on redeploying cash into higher-return projects and narrowing the gap between ROIC and WACC. The VTO may simplify Genting’s structure, but only higher returns — not bigger bets — can fix a low-return giant.

body: The ROIC is low because the company operates in a heavy-asset industry, but ROIC doesn’t account for asset appreciation. if including the asset appreciation actually will be more . If you use ROIC to measure their performance, it won’t fully reflect their real performance, because ROIC is based on net profit after tax. You should use EBITDA instead.

author: ImCK
body: Genting’s pattern is similar to a technology stock the key focus should be on revenue growth, because revenue never lies. If ROIC is low but revenue continues to grow, it means the company is still in an expansion phase, reinvesting heavily to build future capacity and market share. I always compare depreciation growth with revenue and EBITDA growth. If depreciation is rising at a similar pace, it means the company’s growth is asset-driven and still in an expansion phase. But if revenue and EBITDA grow faster than depreciation, it indicates improving capital efficiency and stronger returns on past investments. Example GENTING U.S BAHAMAS SEGMENT EBITDA: 1,038.0 DEPRECIATE: 1,298.3 in ROIC it will directly become negative 😂

author: Michaelchan2024
body: EBITDA shows how much cash-flow-like profit the company generates before interest, tax, depreciation & amortisation. It’s a good measure of operational performance, but does not reflect how well the capital is being used (i.e., it ignores cost of capital, debt, tax, depreciation). So for GenM: strong EBITDA but low ROIC = the company is generating cash, but relative to its capital base the returns are weak.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: ROIC → best for measuring longterm value creation and capital efficiency. EBITDA → best for measuring short term operational performance and cash flow potential.

body: A complete, accurate timeline of Genting Singapore, from its early phase to the present, including key corporate and stock milestones: Genting Singapore was originally listed as Genting International in the 1980s. In 2004–2005, Genting Berhad reorganized its Singapore operations. December 2005: Genting Singapore was listed on SGX via a reverse takeover of Star Cruises, consolidating Genting’s cruise and resort operations under a single listed company.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: Early 2000s: Preparing for Integrated Resorts 2000–2003: Strengthening operational capability in Singapore and Asia; improving management structure and corporate governance. 2003–2005: Strategic investments in hotel, casino, and legal readiness in Singapore for integrated resort licensing. December 2005: Genting Singapore was listed on SGX via a reverse takeover of Star Cruises, not relisted. It’s technically a new listing through consolidation, rather than a relisting of an existing SGX company. 2006–2010: Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) Development December 2006: Genting Singapore awarded Resorts World Sentosa license (Singapore’s first integrated resort with casino, hotels, and Universal Studios Singapore). 2007–2009: Construction phase of RWS; operational and financial resources concentrated on development. 2010 (February 14): Official opening of RWS, boosting revenue and investor confidence. --- 2010–2011: Market Reaction Share price and market capitalization increased significantly due to RWS opening and successful operations. Positive sentiment for Genting Berhad as a result of Genting Singapore’s performance. --- 2011–2015: Expansion & Growth RWS continued to expand offerings with new attractions and events. Genting Singapore strengthened position as a leading integrated resort operator in Singapore. Stable financial performance supported Genting Berhad’s long-term valuation. --- 2016–2020: Consolidation & Regional Focus Focus on operational efficiency and maximizing returns from RWS. Genting Singapore explored regional opportunities but maintained Singapore as its primary revenue driver. --- 2021–Present: Strategic Projects & Global Positioning Continued innovation and expansion at RWS. Plays a key role in Genting Group’s global strategy, including potential privatizations, integrated resort investments, and international expansions. Remains a core asset driving Genting Berhad’s cash flow, valuation, and strategic flexibility
